target: Every branch of the parser that can change source -> canonical AST output is pinned by a golden assertion.
rules: A measured file with no `unpinned` entry must be fully covered on every required metric.
An `unpinned` entry is the maximum permitted number of unpinned lines, functions, and branches for that file; unprotected surface may only shrink.

An intended behaviour change may move which code the pinning corpus reaches, growing an entry without any protection having eroded. That is the one case where an entry may increase: the increase is recorded with its cause in the CHANGELOG entry of the release that caused it and reviewed as part of the change. Growth with no such cause is a regression.
`unpinned` shrinks by adding corpus inputs that pin behaviour, not by adding tests that merely execute the code. A test that raises coverage without asserting parse output does not pay it down.

An `exempt` entry removes a file from measurement and is legitimate only when no source input can reach the file at all. Generated code is not exemptible: nobody reviews it, so its behaviour needs pinning more than hand-written code, not less.
Code that no source input can reach is a defect or dead code to be decided on, never an `unpinned` entry: recording it would promise a test that cannot be written.

A platform that cannot produce a required metric declares it in `unsupportedMetrics` with a reason; the gate fails if a required metric turns up with no counters at all, and fails again if an unsupported one turns up with data.

unsupportedMetrics.reason: llvm-cov emits no branch regions for Swift: SwiftPM's coverage instrumentation produces line, function, and region counters only. Line and function coverage carry this platform's gate until the toolchain grows branch support.

pathRewrite.reason: The suites import the emitted module, and tsc maps src/<name>.ts to dist/<name>.js one to one. Type-only constructs emit nothing, so full coverage of the output is full coverage of every executable construct in the reviewed source.

purpose: This gate measures which BINDING code a golden assertion pins. It is not a code-quality score and must never be used to record current behaviour as acceptable. Producers run only the suites that assert parse output, so a covered branch is one a golden assertion would catch changing, and an uncovered branch is behaviour a rewrite can alter silently. The c-host platform is gone: it ratcheted line and branch counts per C file, and those files are the ones a Rust engine replaces, so the ledger could not outlive the rewrite it was meant to protect. What protects the engine across that rewrite is the source-to-AST corpus — spec, pathological, entity, extension-order, equivalence, fuzz, and both parity oracles.
